summary:
[reference generation] A fifteen-second vertical cinematic LIVE-ACTION take of Dante performing with Nevan in the opera house, at natural real-time speed.

retention_analysis:
Fully preserve <Subject 1> face, hair, anatomy, costume and materials from <Picture 1>. Fully preserve <Subject 2> short-neck silhouette, flat body, asymmetrical tips, apertures and contact points throughout every angle. Fully preserve <Subject 3> architecture, lighting and stage geography. The picture is an appearance reference, not a frozen pose: Dante performs the action described below. Natural human skin, individual hair strands, weighted worn leather and solid metallic violet prop. No cartoon, plastic skin, game rendering, robot or costume redesign. Five fingers per hand. RIGHT hand physically strums the existing compact string bed; LEFT hand grips the existing SHORT neck. No band, crowd, microphone, extra actor, singing, speech, logos, subtitles or text.

detailed_description:
[Shot 1] 00:00-00:15, one uninterrupted front three-quarter shot of the same opera stage. Open on Dante front three-quarter with boots planted, Nevan across his waist, right hand strumming and left hand on the short neck, already in the energetic riff. Do NOT copy the tight framing of the reference image. Actor is SMALL inside the large stage, occupying only the central60percent of frame height; the entire guitar fits within the central70percent of frame width with a broad empty margin at BOTH sides. This is a distant full-stage composition, never a medium shot. The full head, boots, hands and ALL blade tips stay inside the frame with substantial extra space above his head. The camera immediately dollies backward for3seconds before the guitar rises, then tracks gently along the stage front to follow him. Maintain the stage axis and legible body action. No cut, zoom-in, compensating full camera orbit or slow motion.
00:00-00:03: Continue the same confident E-minor performance. Right wrist articulates the phrase against the compact string bed; left hand controls the short neck. Dante flexes his knees, loads his weight onto the rear boot and looks toward the rising headpiece. Leather and hair lag behind the body.
00:03-00:07: In one physically continuous lift, both arms raise the ENTIRE rigid Nevan above his forehead and around the outside of his head into the classic behind-the-head playing position. The broad blade body travels through free air above and behind the shoulders; it never passes through his skull, hair, upper arms or coat. LEFT glove maintains the neck grip and RIGHT glove stays associated with the same string bed. The short neck, spear headpiece and three asymmetric body tips retain their exact shape and size.
00:07-00:10: Dante plays a brief emphatic phrase behind his head, elbows elevated and torso tilted, with a mischievous confident expression. His wrists do actual string work while his knees support the lean. Then he brings the solid instrument back out around the side of his head into the front waist-height playing position, showing its causal travel without a hidden reset. No aerial flip, weapon throw or extra guitar.
00:10-00:12.5: With Nevan secure in front, he performs ONE full grounded body pivot, pushing off a planted boot and stepping around the support foot until he faces front again. This is Dante actually turning, not the camera orbiting a static actor. The coat fans outward AFTER the torso, boots remain in contact with the floor and all prop extremities remain framed. Both hands retain the one guitar.
00:12.5-00:15: Dante bends through hips and knees, lowers onto both knees with a short controlled forward slide, and strikes a final ringing power chord as his knees meet the floor. Body deceleration and coat settling follow the contact. Nevan remains rigid in front/along his left side; hand ownership stays clear. The camera retreats slightly with the slide to protect the headpiece. End with the final chord decaying and Dante recovering from the knee landing, fabric and hair still settling, not a frozen image. No sudden full-body rotation, jump, teleport or long victory hold after the landing.

No copied game recording, no voice, no drums, no bass backing band, no applause or crowd. The guitar is the only musical source.
